verses.text: Di revelation wey Habakkuk di prophet see.
Di Lord, how long I go dey cry, and you no go hear? I cry out to you, “Violence!” and you no go save?
Why you dey show me iniquity, and dey look perversity? Because destruction and violence dey before me. Strife dey, and contention dey rise up.
So di law don lose power, and justice no dey ever come out; because di wicked dey surround di righteous. So justice dey come out twisted.
“Look among di nations, watch, wonder, and dey astonished! Because I dey do one work for una days, wey una no go believe even if dem tell una.”
“Because look, I dey raise up di Chaldeans, dat bitter and hasty nation, wey dey march through di breadth of di earth, to possess dwelling places wey no belong to dem.”
“Dem dey awesome and dreadful. Dem judgment and dem dignity dey come from dem own selves.”
“Dem horses dey faster pass leopards, and dem dey more fierce pass evening wolves. Dem horsemen dey spread out. Yes, dem horsemen dey come from far. Dem dey fly like eagle wey dey hurry to devour.”
“All of dem dey come for violence. Dem hordes dey face forward. Dem dey gather prisoners like sand.”
“Yes, e dey scoff at kings, and princes na mockery to am. E dey laugh at every stronghold; because e dey heap up dust, and take am.”
“Den e dey sweep pass like wind, and dey continue. E guilty truly, di one wey im own might na im god.”
You no dey from everlasting, di Lord my God, my Holy One? We no go die. Di Lord, you don appoint am for judgment. You, Rock, don establish am to punish.

You wey get eyes wey pure pass to see evil, and wey no fit look perversity, why you dey tolerate dem wey dey deal treacherously, and you dey keep quiet when di wicked swallow di man wey righteous pass am,
And you dey make men like di fish of di sea, like di creeping things, wey no get ruler over dem?
E dey take up all of dem with hook. E dey catch dem inside im net, and gather dem inside im dragnet. So e dey rejoice and e glad.
So e dey sacrifice to im net, and burn incense to im dragnet; because by dem im portion rich, and im food plenty.
E go dey empty im net all di time because of dis, and e no go spare to kill di nations all di time?
I go stand for my watch, and put myself for di tower, and I go look out to see wetin e go talk to me, and wetin I go answer about my complaint.
Di Lord answer me and talk say, “Write di vision, and make am plain for tablets, so that di one wey dey run fit read am.”
“Because di vision still dey wait for di appointed time, and e dey hurry toward di end, and e no go prove false. Even if e take time, wait for am; because e go surely come. E no go delay.”
“Look, im soul dey puff up. E no upright inside am; but di righteous go live by im faith.”

“Yes, moreover, wine dey treacherous, na proud man, and e no dey stay for house; wey dey make im desire wide like Sheol, and e be like death, and e no fit dey satisfied, but e dey gather to imself all nations, and heap to imself all peoples.”

“Dem all no go take up parable against am, and mocking proverb against am, and talk say, ‘Woe dey for di one wey dey increase wetin no belong to am, and wey dey enrich imself by extortion! How long?’”
“Your debtors no go rise up suddenly, and wake up dem wey go make you tremble? You go be dem prey.”

“Because you don plunder plenty nations, all di remnant of di peoples go plunder you, because of men blood, and for di violence wey dem do to di country, to di city and to all wey dey live inside am.”
“Woe dey for di one wey get evil gain for im house, so that e go set im nest high, so that dem go save am from di hand of evil!”
“You don plan shame for your house, by cutting off plenty peoples, and you don sin against your soul.”
“Because di stone go cry out from di wall, and di beam from di woodwork go answer am.”
“Woe dey for di one wey build town with blood, and establish city by iniquity!”
“Look, no be from di Lord of Armies e dey come say di peoples dey labor for di fire, and di nations dey tire demself for vanity?”
“Because di earth go full with di knowledge of di glory of di Lord, as di waters cover di sea.”
“Woe dey for di one wey dey give im neighbor drink, dey pour out your wrath, and also make am drunk, so that you go look dem nakedness!”
“You don full with shame, no be glory. You too, drink, and make your uncircumcision show! Di cup of di Lord right hand go come round to you, and complete shame go dey on your glory.”

“Because di violence wey dem do to Lebanon go cover you, and di destruction of di animals, wey make dem afraid; because of men blood, and for di violence wey dem do to di country, to di city and to all wey dey live inside am.”
“Wetin di engraved image dey profit, wey im maker engrave; di molten image, even di teacher of lies, say di one wey shape im form dey trust am, to make idols wey no fit talk?”
“Woe dey for di one wey talk say to di wood, ‘Wake up!’ or to di stone wey no fit talk, ‘Rise!’ Dis one fit teach? Look, dem don cover am with gold and silver, and breath no dey inside am at all.”
“But di Lord dey inside im holy temple. Make all di earth keep quiet before am.”
Dis na prayer of Habakkuk di prophet, set to Shigionoth.
Di Lord, I don hear about your fame. I dey stand in awe of your deeds, di Lord. Revive your work for di middle of di years. For di middle of di years make am known. For wrath, remember mercy.
God come from Teman, di Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. Im glory cover di heavens. Di earth full with im praise.
Im splendor dey like di light. E get rays wey dey come from im hand, and na dat place im power dey hide.
Plague dey go before am, and pestilence dey follow im feet.
E stand, and shake di earth. E look, and make di nations tremble. Di ancient mountains scatter. Di age-old hills collapse. Im ways dey eternal.
I see di tents of Cushan inside trouble. Di dwellings of di land of Midian tremble.
Di Lord dey angry with di rivers? Your anger dey against di rivers, or your wrath against di sea, say you ride on your horses, on your chariots of salvation?
Dem don strip your bow bare. Di oaths to di tribes dey sure. Selah. You split di earth with rivers.
Di mountains see you, and writhe. Di tempest of waters pass by. Di deep raise im voice, and lift up im hands high.
Di sun and moon stand still for dem place. For di light of your arrows dem move, for di shining of your glittering spear.
You march through di land with fury. You thresh di nations with anger.
You come out for di salvation of your people, for di salvation of your anointed. You crush di head of di land of wickedness. You lay am bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
You pierce di heads of im warriors with dem own spears. Dem come like whirlwind to scatter me. Dem rejoicing na like to devour di wretched ones for secret.
You trample di sea with your horses, dey churn di great waters.

I hear, and my belly tremble, my lips quiver at di voice. Rottenness dey enter my bones, and I tremble for my place; because I must wait quietly for di day of trouble, for di coming up of di people wey go invade us.
Because even if di fig tree no flourish, and fruit no dey inside di vines; di labor of di olive fail, di fields give no food; di flocks don cut off from di fold, and herd no dey inside di stalls:
Yet I go rejoice for di Lord. I go dey joyful for di God of my salvation!
Di Lord God na my strength. E dey make my feet like deer feet, and e dey enable me to walk for di heights. For di music director, on my stringed instruments.
